lines.question: What did Owen do at LexisNexis?

hits.title: LexisNexis Risk Solutions
hits.heading: Placement and continuing work
hits.text: Owen worked as a Data Scientist on industrial placement at LexisNexis Risk Solutions from July 2025 to August 2026, then continued as an AI engineering contractor from August 2026. His owner-supplied account describes two fraud-model optimisations, financial-data analysis using Python, SQL and Snowflake, and research into self-supervised representations. Much of his Lexis work is customer-facing.

hits.title: LexisNexis Risk Solutions
hits.heading: Evidence and disclosure
hits.text: These employment and contribution claims are Owen’s account, not independently verified performance results. Employer code, transaction data, customer identities and internal evaluation results are not published here. Production monitoring and retraining remain gaps in the experience described; this page does not claim ownership of a deployed monitoring or retraining system.

hits.title: LexisNexis Risk Solutions
hits.heading: From demonstration to internal pilot
hits.text: According to Owen’s account, he architected an AI workflow intended for organisation-wide use, built an end-to-end demonstration and presented the concept, value and scaling approach to senior stakeholders. He was retained to develop a funded internal pilot toward production. Persistent state, audit trails and human-review gates are part of the described approach. Intended scope does not establish organisation-wide deployment or tested production scale.

hits.title: LexisNexis Risk Solutions
hits.heading: ML tooling for the team
hits.text: Owen reports responsibility for ML tooling, including improving the speed, quality and ease of use of LightGBM rule mining for the team’s data scientists. No numerical speed-up, quality metric or customer-specific result is supplied. Detailed case studies still need a publishable problem statement, personal contribution, constraints and outcome evidence.
